items.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022
items.q: when I moved back to Boston after leaving Dave Brubeck in 1981

ctx.x: Did you have to do some serious — well let me rephrase. I’m going to guess that maybe you started teaching a few private lessons and then to move to a university level did you have to codify some of your own methods and prove to some committee that you were worthy of being there?

Actually no I didn’t. I had already codified a lot of — because I had, when I moved back to Boston after leaving Dave Brubeck in 1981, the end of ’81, I put up little flyers and in a short amount of time I had a two year waiting list. Two years. And if you want to study with me okay you can but you’re on a list, two years. And it really was a two year waiting list. And so after years of doing that and having all the teachers from Berklee © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

study with me — and not all of them but most of them you know, and they’re teaching my stuff and I didn’t even think about it. This is what I teach. And the only reason I was good at it was because I taught myself. Nobody showed me so I had to learn how to play. And it’s the only thing I wanted to do is be a better player. So I would get systems for myself to practice. But then Berklee called me up and offered me a position for low bread. And I said I don’t even have to leave my apartment, I’ve got a two year…
